nodes.title: `--attach` requires write access, so outside reporters cannot attach screenshots

nodes.bodyText:
Thanks for the detailed writeup. I'm suggesting the enhancement label: this describes a real gap in the recently-shipped --attach feature (#13256/#14186) where the upload endpoint's permission check (ADMIN/MAINTAIN/WRITE) excludes read-only outside reporters from attaching files, even though the same accounts can upload via the web UI. I checked for duplicates and didn't find an exact match — #14194 and #12960 request the underlying attach capability itself, which has since shipped, so this is a distinct follow-up about the permission requirement and its documentation. A maintainer should confirm whether the READ/TRIAGE restriction is enforced by the platform API itself or is a CLI-side choice, since that determines whether points 1–2 are actionable here versus upstream, though point 3 (documenting the requirement in --attach help) seems actionable regardless.

Improve handling of action results ZIP archives generated by the new service

nodes.bodyText: Any plans to work on this issue? A month later it's still a problem.

Thanks for the nudge, @andykingit! 🙏 This issue has been discussed in the team and it's under our radar to bring it into our planning after we're done with some other stuff. Also, since this is a bit of integration issue, we're following up with the other stakeholders. I cannot give you an estimate here, though.

@ryan-williams, @kperkins-godaddy, @andykingit, @richmondjerry, @dlvhdr, @ptorgalmath-gpsw we're implementing a fallback approach (stated in #11118 and #11169, and implemented in #11172) for when gh couldn't find the logs in the downloaded ZIP archive. It's not a replacement for this issue, of course, but will fix the use cases. You're welcome to build gh from the PR's branch and test it on your end.
Hey @babakks, I just confirmed, PR #11172 works great! I can fetch all jobs' logs.

Still reproducible on gh version 2.103.3 (2026-10-26).
Since the API fallback (#11172), logs are now printed, but for any reusable-workflow job (named <caller> / <callee>) every line is labelled UNKNOWN STEP, because the step files in the ZIP are never matched.
Example: job deploy / scan (env: prod) is stored in the ZIP as deploy _ scan (env prod)/5_<step name>.txt, but getJobNameForLogFilename in pkg/cmd/run/view/logs.go deletes the / and searches for deploy  scan (env prod) (double space), so neither the job file nor any step file matches.
Replacing / with _ instead of deleting it (in getJobNameForLogFilename) matches the step files in the ZIP for our runs, so --log-failed would show real step names again.

Another data point, from a private repository, so no runs I can link. This one has no / in the job name, and the output is partial rather than empty.
gh version 2.103.2 (2026-10-23) on Linux. Two pull_request runs of the same workflow in the same repository, both attempt 1, an hour apart, each with one job named Build, typecheck, test (npm):

Run 1. The archive from GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{id}/logs holds only Build, typecheck, test (npm)/system.txt and the top-level 0_Build, typecheck, test (npm).txt (242,885 bytes). gh run view <id> --log prints the whole job, 1601 lines.
Run 2. The archive holds the same top-level 0_…txt (242,978 bytes) plus per-step files: 1_Set up job.txt, 2_Run actions_checkout@v7.txt, 3_Run actions_setup-node@v7.txt, 4_Run npm ci.txt, 5_Run npm run build.txt, 6_Run npm run typecheck.txt, 7_…, 8_…, 9_…, 10_Run npm test.txt (221,105 bytes), then 18_… to 21_Complete job.txt. The jobs API lists steps 1–10 and 18–21, all success. gh run view <id> --log prints 89 lines covering steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 only, and exits 0. Step 2 is dropped, and so is everything from step 6 on, the 221 KB step 10 included. Re-running the command gives the same output.

GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/{job_id}/logs returns the complete log for run 2's job. Through gh api that needs --allow-escape-sequences, because the log contains ANSI colour codes.
So the per-step layout is not all-or-nothing: some step files are matched and others silently skipped, while the exit status stays 0. For tooling that parses --log output (we read test counts from it), that is worse than an empty result, since nothing signals that the log is incomplete. In both layouts the top-level 0_<job>.txt held the full log, which may be the more reliable source when it is present.

nodes.title: gh pr close --comment silently discards the comment when PR is already closed or merged

nodes.bodyText:
Verified against the current close.go source: in closeRun, the !pr.IsOpen() branch prints the "already closed" warning and return nils before opts.HttpClient() is called and before shared.CommentableRun executes, so --comment is silently dropped with exit code 0 — matching the reporter's description. This is the same root cause already tracked and confirmed for gh issue close in #14152 (which explicitly notes the gh pr close case as an unreproduced source-read finding), so I'm suggesting duplicate alongside bug and gh-pr. A maintainer should confirm whether this should be folded into #14152's fix or handled as a follow-up PR for the pr close command specifically.

Generated by Issue Triage (skills-driven) for #14374 · copilot · auto · 24.4 AIC · ⌖ 2.28 AIC · ⊞ 11.2K · ◷

I'd like to take this. The fix mirrors whatever convention #14152 settles on for issue close: run the --comment through shared.CommentableRun before the already-closed/merged early return in closeRun, so the comment lands and only the state change is skipped. Will open a PR shortly.

Root Cause Analysis
In pkg/cmd/pr/close/close.go (closeRun, lines 77–83), pr.State == "MERGED" and !pr.IsOpen() return early before the if opts.Comment != "" block (shared.CommentableRun, lines 90–104), causing gh pr close --comment to drop the comment when the PR is already closed or merged.
Proposed Fix
Run shared.CommentableRun when opts.Comment != "" prior to the pr.State == "MERGED" / !pr.IsOpen() early return in pkg/cmd/pr/close/close.go.
I have prepared this fix on branch duongynhi000005-oss:fix/issue-14374-pr-close-comment-when-already-closed and can submit a PR if approved.

nodes.title: gh run view --job --log-failed fails on required shared-workflow metadata 404

nodes.bodyText:
Thanks for the detailed repro. I traced this through the source and the cause looks clear: shared.GetRun (shared.go lines 559–592 at commit 4f2cfe9) always calls workflowShared.GetWorkflow(client, repo, result.WorkflowID) right after fetching the run, and returns any error from that call unmodified. For a run whose workflow originates from an organization/enterprise ruleset rather than the consumer repo's own workflow list, that lookup 404s, so GetRun fails before view.go's --log/--log-failed path ever reaches getRunLog/job-log fetching — even though the run and job metadata and logs are otherwise readable. This matches a known pattern already handled more leniently elsewhere: preloadWorkflowNames (shared.go lines ~487–505) explicitly catches a 404 from the same GetWorkflow call for run list and falls back to an empty workflow name instead of failing, but GetRun (used by run view) has no equivalent fallback. I'm suggesting bug, gh-run, and priority-3 (narrow case with a viable gh api workaround) for maintainer review. This is not a duplicate of #9228 (which is about run list/run view generally 404ing on ruleset workflows); this issue is specifically about --log-failed/--log failing even though job logs themselves are fetchable, so a first responder may want to consider making GetRun's workflow-name lookup tolerate a 404 the same way preloadWorkflowNames does.

Generated by Issue Triage (skills-driven) for #14822 · copilot · auto · 79 AIC · ⊞ 4.5K · ◷

Analysis & Proposed Fix
In pkg/cmd/run/shared/shared.go, GetRun always calls workflowShared.GetWorkflow(client, repo, result.WorkflowID) after fetching the run and returns any error from that lookup directly:
workflow, err := workflowShared.GetWorkflow(client, repo, result.WorkflowID)
if err != nil {
    return nil, err
} else {
    result.workflowName = workflow.Name
}
When a workflow run originates from an organization or enterprise ruleset rather than a workflow file in the consumer repository, GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id} returns 404 Not Found even though the run metadata and job logs are readable in the consumer repository. Consequently, gh run view RUN --job JOB --log-failed fails in GetRun before reaching getRunLog.
Notably, preloadWorkflowNames in the same file (pkg/cmd/run/shared/shared.go:460-474) already handles this exact ruleset-workflow case for gh run list by catching api.HTTPError with status 404 and falling back to an empty workflow name.
Proposed Changes

pkg/cmd/run/shared/shared.go (GetRun):

Check var httpErr api.HTTPError when workflowShared.GetWorkflow returns an error; if errors.As(err, &httpErr) && httpErr.StatusCode == http.StatusNotFound, fall back to an empty workflowName instead of failing GetRun.


Tests:

Added TestGetRunWorkflow404 in pkg/cmd/run/shared/shared_test.go.
Added noninteractive with job log-failed when workflow metadata returns 404 (#14822) in pkg/cmd/run/view/view_test.go.



I have verified this fix with go test ./pkg/cmd/run/... on my fork (duongynhi000005-oss/cli-2:fix/run-view-workflow-404, commit 1f1cb05) and would be happy to open a PR if you'd like to assign this issue to me.

Additional reproduction on gh 2.103.1 (macOS), while diagnosing a required shared validate workflow for a merge-group candidate: gh run view RUN --log-failed also fails on the consumer repository's workflow-metadata endpoint with HTTP 404. The same authenticated gh api .../actions/jobs/JOB/logs --allow-escape-sequences successfully retrieved the job log to a file. This occurs for validation as well as the review-gate case above; no separate issue filed.

Additional reproduction on the same environment: gh run view RUN --repo ORG/CONSUMER --json jobs also fails at the shared required workflow metadata lookup with HTTP 404 while the run is in progress. With the same authentication, gh api repos/ORG/CONSUMER/actions/runs/RUN/jobs succeeds and returns current job states. This is therefore not limited to completed runs or log requests. No private repository/run identifiers are included here.

nodes.title: gh issue close --comment silently discards the comment when the issue is already closed, and exits 0

nodes.bodyText:
Thanks for the detailed report, including root cause and reproduction steps. I'm suggesting bug and priority-2 labels: this silently discards the --comment text and reports success (exit 0) on a common automation path (issue already closed by a linked commit), even though the close no-op itself is correct behavior. No duplicate issues were found in a search of open/closed issues. There's already a linked PR (#14160) addressing this, so a maintainer can review that fix directly.

Generated by Issue Triage (skills-driven) · auto · 16.8 AIC · ⌖ 0.568 AIC · ⊞ 9.7K · ◷

Root Cause Analysis
In pkg/cmd/issue/close/close.go (closeRun, lines 117–120), if issue.State == "CLOSED" prints a warning and returns nil before reaching the if opts.Comment != "" block (prShared.CommentableRun, lines 148–162). As a result, any comment passed via gh issue close --comment on an already-closed issue is silently discarded.
Proposed Fix
Execute the if opts.Comment != "" block (prShared.CommentableRun) before the issue.State == "CLOSED" early return in pkg/cmd/issue/close/close.go.
I have prepared this fix on branch duongynhi000005-oss:fix/issue-14152-issue-close-comment-when-already-closed and can open a PR if helpful.

nodes.title: `--attach` cannot work for GitHub App installation tokens — the upload endpoint 404s them even with write access

nodes.bodyText:
Thanks for the detailed report and reproduction. This looks like a legitimate enhancement/documentation request: the --attach allowlist (from #14186) rejects GitHub App installation tokens (ghs_), and you've verified the upload endpoint itself 404s for that token type even with write access. I'm suggesting enhancement (to track widening uploadTokenTypes if the endpoint supports it, or documenting the limitation) and gh-pr since --attach is used in PR/issue workflows. No duplicates found in existing issues (#14194 covers general attachment support and #8747 covers GitHub App auth, but neither addresses this specific token-allowlist/endpoint restriction). A maintainer should confirm whether this is a platform-side restriction to route upstream or a CLI-side allowlist that can be relaxed.

Generated by Issue Triage (skills-driven) for #14309 · copilot · auto · 22.3 AIC · ⌖ 2.2 AIC · ⊞ 9.7K · ◷
Thanks for the request @Ninodevo. This is intended behavior for now, but we may re-evaluate in the future based on demand.

Thank you for your issue! We have categorized it as an enhancement (feature or improvement) request, and it has been added to our backlog. In doing so, we are not committing to implementing this feature at this time, but, we will consider it for future releases based on community feedback and our own product roadmap.
Unless you see the https://github.com/cli/cli/labels/help%20wanted label, we are not currently looking for external contributions for this feature.
If you come across this issue and would like to see it implemented, please add a thumbs up! This will help us prioritize the feature. Please only comment if you have additional information or viewpoints to contribute.

Highlighting that we were attempting to change our awkward media -> S3 -> link -> Github process now to use this, and also found it to be ineffective since bots can't use it (and they do a lot of our visual validation).

While waiting on something first party, gh-image attaches from Actions today. It uses the web upload flow, so no App token is involved: set GH_SESSION_TOKEN from a dedicated bot account.
It also handles logs, zips and PDFs, not just images and video.

+1 this, we are having to do some really silly workarounds and using a dedicated PAT when our whole app functions with app installation tokens. This feels like an arbitrary limitation when installation tokens grant most of the same functionality already.
This makes it much harder for agents to demonstrate on a PR that they've actually verified code works.

@Ninodevo  thanks for posting this. Our security policy prohibits long-lived PATs and OAuth tokens for automation. GitHub App installation tokens are the only credential class we're allowed to use in CI. As written, --attach is unusable for us entirely. The feature is great, but excluding the most secure, most recommended token type makes it a human-only tool. We'd love to adopt it the day ghs_ tokens are supported.

Adding a data point from a team using Amp (ampcode.com) agents in cloud sandboxes. Their GH_TOKEN is a GitHub App user-to-server token (ghu_). Since #14495, gh 2.102+ passes it through, but the upload endpoint still 404s. gh reports that as "attaching files requires write access to the repository", although the user has MAINTAIN.
Our agents verify UI changes with screenshots and recordings, and we would really like them to attach those results to the PR body themselves. Today the only way is a personal PAT stored as a secret per user. That is a lot of friction, and it is a wider credential than an App token. Support for user GitHub Apps (or a narrower upload permission) would make this work out of the box for agent-driven workflows.

+1 this makes it very difficult for agents to add evidence to PRs and we've also had to employ workarounds, or are often just fully blocked. This is available with the PAT authentication, but would much rather use the App connection.

🛑 Requirement: Cover both non-spam exception branches in the evaluator
This criterion requires same-author reposts and cross-author quotations with author-supplied context to remain legitimate. The corpus's only <AUTHOR> case covers the spam branch; existing PASS cases omit <AUTHOR>, so they cannot verify either the author comparison or the context exception once the repost is known to be cross-author. Add explicit PASS fixtures for both cases to prevent legitimate issues from being auto-closed by a future prompt change.
